user.title: EV usage model
user.description: Pick the EV's state-of-charge and plugged-in sensors, then set the pack parameters used to size charging.

data_description.ev_name: Used for entity ids, for example "GAC Aion UT" gives sensor.gac_aion_ut_charge_rate_forecast.
data_description.soc_entity_id: A sensor whose state is the pack percentage (0-100). Its slope drives the drive-power signal.
data_description.plugged_entity_id: A binary sensor that is on while the cable is connected, or a status sensor whose states you map with the three lists below.
data_description.plugged_states: Leave all three lists empty for a binary sensor: "on" means connected. For a status sensor, list every state where the cable is connected, for example plugged_in, waiting, charged, paused.
data_description.unplugged_states: States where the cable is not connected, for example sleep, idle. These win over the plugged-in and charging lists.
data_description.charging_states: States where power is actually flowing, for example charging. A charging state always counts as plugged in too.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable energy in the pack; converts percentage into kW and kWh.
data_description.efficiency_pct: Wall-to-pack efficiency used when converting charge rate into stored energy.
data_description.charge_rate_kw: AC power the EV draws while plugged in; used when no measured history exists.
data_description.buffer_kwh: Extra energy kept above the trip requirement.
data_description.max_soc_pct: Cap for the required state of charge, so an unreachable target never pins charging to the maximum.
data_description.history_days: Days of hour buckets averaged for the forecasts.
data_description.soc_window_minutes: Minutes of state-of-charge movement used for the live power signals.
data_description.horizon_hours: How far ahead the required state of charge looks for trips.

init.title: EV usage model
init.description: Tune the model. Changes apply without recreating the entities; changing the source entities reloads the entry.
